summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable. Studio did not run: the simulation status is skipped, the gate has simulation_allowed false, and comparison_valid is false. The reason given is that a custom experiment needs 1–128 blocks and a power_w object, and the extraction supplied an empty floorplan and empty power map. The paper scenario is the steady-state HotSpot 6.0 per-layer temperature of a TSV-based 3x3x3 3D-NoC (Figure 10), compared with a Monolithic 3D-NoC. The only numeric observable is the text-quoted maximum Monolithic temperature of 351.64 K (78.49 C). Its layer, router and benchmark are not named, and the aggregation is not fully specified. The intended experiment kind was custom_2d_steady, so even if it had run it would have produced a steady result with no transient trace and no bundled EV6/GCC adaptation. There is therefore no Studio temperature to compare with 351.64 K, and no numerical agreement or disagreement can be claimed. The 3D stack physics (three layers, bonding/TIM layers, TSV heat paths, a top-mounted heatsink, a monolithic comparison) cannot be represented by a single-die 2D steady model. The paper's reliability results use Black's model and are not thermal solver outputs. Only qualitative remarks are defensible: in the paper, layer position and TSV or bonding-layer treatment drive temperature differences, which a 2D model would not capture. This assessment does not replicate or validate the paper, and it makes no claim of exact replication.
limitations: Studio was not executed, so no simulated temperature, map or trace exists for this scenario.
The 2D screening verdict is not_2d_applicable. The input gate and scientific gate both failed, independent verification is absent, and comparison_valid is false.

The reported 351.64 K maximum is for the Monolithic 3D-NoC at an unspecified layer, router and benchmark, with unclear aggregation. It cannot be matched to any 2D output in location, aggregation, regime or boundary conditions.

Essential physical mismatches: a 3-layer stack, bonding/TIM layers, TSV effective resistivity, a top heatsink with lower layers cooled through upper layers, and a per-layer observable. None is representable by a steady 2D single-die model.

The inputs are insufficient: no block placement coordinates, no numeric per-router power (Figure 8 is a bar chart only), no layer thicknesses, package or heatsink parameters or ambient temperature, no numeric Figure 10 table, and no packet assets such as HotSpot configs, .flp or .ptrace files.

The evidence items lack valid page or pinned asset locators, and the adversarial methods, code, parameters, config and data checks are unresolved. The reviewer did not approve all extracted claims, and the independent page/asset review is pending.
The linked URLs are background references or design kits (patent, reliability handbooks, NanGate, FreePDK3D45), are not pinned, and do not show that experiment input files exist.

The paper has internal inconsistencies: static power is 7.66e-4 W in the text and 7.64e-4 W in Table 2, and energy per bit is 9.246e-13 in the text and 9.2546e-13 J/bit in the table. The Table 3 resistivity units are printed as mK/W and are unverified.
The paper has no optimizer or controller, so no Studio optimizer or controller mapping applies. The studio_assumptions list is empty and the bundled Studio package/material assumptions are unknown.
